about: Flatness of the promoted Arcturus correction (fit_fts_batch.py --arcturus, 2026-10-29) against the superseded fit_arcturus_batch record and the atlas authors' ratioed spectrum, every page-epoch, with --relative-transmission. Scored before promotion: 'new' was data/corrected/arcturus_solar_era, now data/corrected/atlas; 'old' was the superseded npz rewritten into fit_window's array names, now data/corrected/superseded_pre_solar_era/old_converted_for_scoring. The method text is the scorer's own and names niratl; for this run the authors' series is each page's ratioed column.
method: niratl ships the authors' own corrected solar spectrum (Wallace, Hinkle & Livingston 1993). Ours minus theirs mixes both corrections' errors, so instead each is scored on its own, the same way: at pixels where the model transmission is below 0.97 and the solar model is flat (above 0.995 of its continuum), the rms of the corrected spectrum about a running mean of nearby pixels with neither solar nor telluric absorption. A perfect correction leaves noise there. The first and last 50 pixels are not scored: an edge pixel is inside the neighbouring page too (pages overlap by 5 cm-1), and a fit that leaves edges out should not be judged on them. Nor are pixels below a transmission of 0.15, which the corrected products blank: dividing by a saturated core turns a percent of model error into a spike that can outweigh the rest of a window. Two bins: every telluric pixel (T < 0.97) and the deep ones (T < 0.7).
